scenario_summary: The customer is attempting to access an account without access to registered credentials or an order number and is requesting a refund.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Wei Li and I'm 43. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.

Hello Wei, I understand how frustrating it can be to be locked out of your account while traveling. For your security, I cannot access account details based on name alone, as our Privacy and Data Protection Policy requires at least two unique identifiers to verify ownership. Could you please provide the billing address associated with the account and the approximate date of the transaction you are looking to have refunded?
Oh, I see. The billing address would be 123 Maple Street, Springfield. And I believe the purchase was made around the 15th of last month, maybe for about $45?

Thank you for that information, Wei. I have located a profile matching that address. To finalize verification, I have just sent a one-time passcode to the recovery method on file, which appears to be a phone number ending in -4492. Could you please confirm if you have access to that device to provide the code?
Actually, that's my old work phone, and I don't have it with me. Is there any other way? I really need that refund processed today.

I apologize for the inconvenience, but per our Account Recovery Security Protocol, we cannot bypass multi-factor authentication for financial inquiries or refunds without the registered device or a verified email address. Since you are unable to access the registered recovery method, I will need to escalate this to our Identity Verification Team. They can perform a manual identity review using alternative documentation. Would you like me to initiate that secure ticket for you now?
That sounds like the only way forward. Yes, please go ahead and start that process.

I have successfully opened case #88291 for you. A specialist will contact you via the email address you provide to them to request a secure upload of a government-issued ID. Once your identity is confirmed through that channel, they will be able to assist you with the refund request. You should receive a confirmation email shortly.

escalation_reason: Customer failed multi-factor authentication and could not verify ownership of the account via the registered recovery phone number, requiring manual identity verification by a specialized team.
